title: Study Path: Well-rounded IT & CS
oneLiner: A week-by-week route through the whole academy for broad, practical computing knowledge: hardware, programming, operating systems, networks, security, Linux, databases, Git, systems and AI.

title: The Math You Need: Powers, Logarithms and Sums
oneLiner: Three pieces of school math that explain most of computing's numbers: powers of two, logarithms as "how many halvings", and the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n.

title: Data Types: Numbers, Text and True/False
oneLiner: Every value in a program has a type that decides how it's stored in bits and what you can do with it, and a fixed-size integer can overflow.

title: Functions, Memory and the Call Stack
oneLiner: What happens in memory when one function calls another, why a copied list can change "by itself", and how a function can call itself (recursion).

title: Computer Architecture: CPU, GPU, RAM, Storage & the OS
oneLiner: The physical pieces of a computer, what each one actually does, and the layer (the OS) that connects them to the code you write.

title: Logic Gates: AND, OR, XOR & Friends
oneLiner: Every computation a CPU does eventually reduces to these tiny truth-table circuits, wired together by the billions.

title: Dynamic Arrays: How They Grow
oneLiner: A resizable array (List<T>, ArrayList, Python's list) isn't magic -- it's a fixed-size array underneath that gets replaced with a bigger one when it fills up.

title: Bits, Bytes & Number Bases
oneLiner: Every number in a computer is bits -- binary, decimal, and hex are just three readings of the same bit pattern.

title: Floating Point: IEEE-754
oneLiner: A number like 3.5 is stored as three fields of bits, a sign, an exponent and a mantissa, which is exactly why 0.1 + 0.2 isn't 0.3.

title: Byte Order: Little vs Big Endian
oneLiner: The same multi-byte number gets stored in opposite byte order depending on the machine -- and mixing them up is a real, recurring bug.

title: CPU Scheduling: FCFS, SJF, Round Robin and Priority
oneLiner: How the OS decides which ready process (running program) gets the CPU next, and how that choice changes waiting time, response time and fairness.

title: User Mode, Kernel Mode, System Calls and Interrupts
oneLiner: Why your code can't touch the disk directly, how it asks the kernel to, and how hardware gets the CPU's attention.

title: What Happens When You Run a Program
oneLiner: From typing ./hello to the shell prompt coming back: fork, exec, the loader, main, exit and the process lifecycle.

title: Compiled vs Interpreted: How C# and Python Run
oneLiner: Roslyn to IL to JIT or AOT for C#, source to bytecode on a virtual machine for Python, and why "compiled language" is the wrong question.

title: Linkers, Libraries and Loading
oneLiner: How separately compiled files become one program, what "undefined reference" really means, and static vs dynamic libraries.

title: Text Encoding: ASCII, Unicode, UTF-8 and UTF-16
oneLiner: Characters are numbers called code points, encodings turn them into bytes, and that is why "string length" has three different answers.

title: Start Here: C# and Python Side by Side

title: Variables, Types and Expressions

title: Temperature Conversion with Rounding

title: Reverse the Words

title: Running Total

title: Find the First Position of a Value

title: Functions

title: Word Frequency

title: Values in Both Lists
oneLiner: Return the values that appear in both lists, once each, in the order they first appear in the first list.

title: Errors and Exceptions

title: Add Up the Valid Numbers

oneLiner: Write your first class: a constructor that stores width and height, and three methods that use them.

title: Records, Dataclasses and Equality

title: Distinct Points with a Record
oneLiner: Turn a plain Point class into a record (or frozen dataclass) so equal points really are equal, then remove duplicates with a set.

title: Immutability, Values and References

title: Format a Report Line
oneLiner: Build one fixed-width line of a report: a left-aligned name, a right-aligned quantity, and two money columns with two decimals.

title: Parse key=value Settings

title: Unit Testing with xUnit and pytest
oneLiner: Writing your first unit tests: arrange, act, assert, xUnit's Fact and Theory next to pytest functions and parametrize, testing for exceptions, per-test setup with constructors and fixtures, running the tests and reading failures.

title: Modules, Namespaces and Packages
oneLiner: Organising code across files: C# namespaces, using and assemblies, Python modules, packages and imports, the entry point and if __name__ == "__main__", and installing packages with NuGet and pip in a virtual environment.

oneLiner: Add up the semicolon-separated numbers in a line by walking it with indexes and slicing a ReadOnlySpan<char>, instead of splitting it into new strings.

title: Threads, Locks, the GIL and Parallelism
oneLiner: Running work at the same time: threads and race conditions, locks and atomic operations, the GIL and why Python uses processes for CPU-bound work, thread pools, Parallel.For, thread-safe collections, producer-consumer queues and deadlocks.

title: Async in Depth: Cancellation, Timeouts and Streams
oneLiner: What await does under the hood (the event loop and the compiler's state machine), cooperative cancellation with CancellationToken and task.cancel, timeouts, WhenAny and as_completed, limiting concurrency with semaphores, async streams, and handling several failures.

oneLiner: Wrapping functions with Python decorators and C# delegates, decorators with settings and caching, guaranteed clean-up with using and IDisposable versus with and context managers, @contextmanager and ExitStack, and how C# attributes differ from decorators.

oneLiner: Open a list of resources, do the work, and close every resource that was opened, newest first, even when opening one of them or the work itself fails.

title: Route Commands with List Patterns
oneLiner: Turn operator commands such as start P1, set FT-1 42 and alarm ack 3 7 into responses with one switch expression or match statement over the list of words.

title: Shipping Rates with Patterns

oneLiner: Pure functions and immutable data (records with with, frozen dataclasses, immutable collections), LINQ pipelines versus generator chains, folds, the itertools toolbox and its LINQ equivalents, partial application and composition.

oneLiner: BFS finds the shortest path by HOP COUNT; Dijkstra finds it by total WEIGHT, always finalizing whichever undiscovered node currently has the smallest known distance next.

title: Transfer: Network Delay Time
oneLiner: A signal leaves one node and travels along directed, timed links. How long until every node has it? Dijkstra, then one more question about its answer.

title: Sorting: Bubble Sort
oneLiner: Repeatedly compare neighbors and swap if they're out of order -- the biggest unsorted value "bubbles" to the end each pass.

title: Sorting: Insertion Sort
oneLiner: Grow a sorted prefix one element at a time, sliding each new element back to where it belongs.

title: Sorting: Selection Sort
oneLiner: Repeatedly find the smallest remaining value and swap it into place -- the opposite instinct from bubble sort's constant neighbor-swapping.

title: Sorting: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
oneLiner: The one move at the heart of merge sort: given two already-sorted lists, weave them into one sorted list in a single pass.

title: Sorting: Quick Sort Partition
oneLiner: The core move behind quicksort: pick a pivot, then rearrange so everything smaller ends up left of it and everything bigger ends up right.

title: Dynamic Programming: Fibonacci with Memoization
oneLiner: Same recursive fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2) as before -- but check a cache before recursing, and the exponential blowup disappears.

title: Dynamic Programming: Climbing Stairs (Bottom-Up)
oneLiner: How many distinct ways to climb n stairs, taking 1 or 2 steps at a time? Build the answer bottom-up in an array instead of recursing top-down.

title: Dynamic Programming: Longest Increasing Subsequence
oneLiner: For every index, the best increasing run ENDING there only depends on the best runs ending at every SMALLER, earlier value -- the same overlapping-subproblem shape as Climbing Stairs, one dimension wider.

title: Interval DP: Longest Palindromic Substring
oneLiner: Whether a whole SUBSTRING is a palindrome depends on whether the substring one character shorter, INSIDE it, already was -- the interval-DP shape: solve small ranges first, use them to answer bigger ranges.

title: Binary Search: Find a Target
oneLiner: Cut the search space in half every step -- O(log n) instead of O(n), but only works on sorted data.

title: Binary Search: Find First and Last Position
oneLiner: The same divide-in-half idea, aimed at a BOUNDARY instead of one exact match -- find where a value's range starts and ends.

title: Binary Search on Answer: Minimum Eating Speed
oneLiner: Not every binary search hunts through an array -- this one hunts through the space of POSSIBLE ANSWERS for the smallest one that actually works.

title: Binary Search: Search a Rotated Sorted Array
oneLiner: A sorted array that was rotated is no longer sorted, but whichever way you cut it at the midpoint, at least one half still is.

title: Transfer: Find the Minimum of a Rotated Sorted Array
oneLiner: No target this time: find the smallest value of a rotated sorted array in O(log n) by keeping whichever half still holds the drop.

title: Binary Search on Answer: Split Array Largest Sum
oneLiner: Instead of choosing where to cut, guess the largest allowed part sum and check greedily whether k parts are enough; then binary search the guess.

title: Two Pointers: Two Sum on a Sorted Array
oneLiner: Same "find a pair that sums to target" shape as Hash Map Two Sum -- but sorted input means zero extra memory.

title: Transfer: 3Sum, Every Triplet That Sums to Zero
oneLiner: Find every distinct triplet that adds up to 0. Sort once, fix the first number, and the rest is the sorted Two Sum scan you already know.

title: Two Pointers: Trapping Rain Water
oneLiner: Water above a bar is min(tallest to its left, tallest to its right) minus its height; two pointers find that min without extra arrays.

title: Fast & Slow Pointers: Find the Middle of a Linked List
oneLiner: Two pointers moving at different speeds down the SAME list -- when the fast one reaches the end, the slow one is sitting exactly at the middle.

title: Linked List Pointers: Reverse a Singly Linked List
oneLiner: Walk the list once with three pointers (prev, curr, next) and flip each node's Next to point backward.

title: Transfer: Reverse Part of a Linked List
oneLiner: Reverse only the nodes from position left to position right. The same pointer flip as before, plus two reconnections, and a dummy node so left = 1 is not a special case.

title: Fast & Slow Pointers: Find Where a Cycle Starts
oneLiner: Floyd's algorithm in two phases: let fast and slow meet inside the loop, then walk one pointer from the head and one from the meeting point until they meet at the cycle's entrance.

title: Two Pointers: Remove the Nth Node From the End
oneLiner: Start two pointers at a dummy node, move the lead n + 1 steps ahead, then move both until the lead falls off the end: the trailing pointer is right before the node to delete.

title: Linked List Pointers: Merge Two Sorted Lists
oneLiner: Splice the existing nodes into one sorted list: a dummy head, a tail pointer, and at each step attach whichever list's front node is smaller.

title: Sliding Window: Max Sum Subarray of Size K
oneLiner: Don't recompute the whole window every time -- slide it: subtract what leaves, add what enters.

title: Sliding Window (Variable Size): Longest Substring Without Repeats
oneLiner: Grow the window on the right; when it breaks the rule, shrink it from the left until it's valid again.

title: Transfer: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
oneLiner: Change at most k letters to get the longest run of one letter. Same variable window as the no-repeats lesson; only the rule it keeps changes.

title: Sliding Window: Minimum Window Substring
oneLiner: Grow the window to the right until it covers every character of t, then shrink it from the left for as long as it still does.

title: Monotonic Stack: Find the Next Greater Element
oneLiner: For every element, find the next one to its right that's bigger -- a stack that only ever holds a decreasing sequence answers this for the WHOLE array in one pass.

title: Transfer: Daily Temperatures
oneLiner: For each day, how many days until a warmer one? The next greater element again, but the answer is a distance, so the stack has to remember positions.

title: Monotonic Deque: Sliding Window Maximum
oneLiner: The maximum of every window of size k, in one pass -- keep a deque of indices whose values only decrease from front to back.

title: Prefix Sums: Answer Range-Sum Queries in O(1)
oneLiner: Precompute running totals once, and any "sum of elements from i to j" becomes a single subtraction instead of a fresh loop.

title: Transfer: Count Subarrays That Sum to K
oneLiner: Count the contiguous runs that add up to k, negatives allowed, in one pass: Two Sum's lookup, run on prefix sums.

title: Merge Intervals: Combine Everything That Overlaps
oneLiner: Sort by start time first, then a single left-to-right pass is enough to merge every overlapping interval -- no interval needs to be revisited once merged.

title: Transfer: Intersect Two Interval Lists
oneLiner: Two people's busy times, each sorted and non-overlapping. Return the times both are busy, in one pass with a pointer into each list.

title: Merge Intervals: Insert an Interval
oneLiner: The list is already sorted and non-overlapping, so one O(n) pass splits it into three runs: before the new interval, overlapping it, and after it.

title: Sweep Line: Minimum Meeting Rooms
oneLiner: The number of rooms you need is the largest number of meetings running at the same moment: sweep through the start and end times in order and track how many are open.

title: Greedy: Non-overlapping Intervals
oneLiner: To remove as few intervals as possible, keep as many as possible: sort by END time and always keep the interval that finishes earliest.

title: Top-K Elements: Use a Heap Instead of Fully Sorting
oneLiner: Need only the K largest (or smallest) values out of n? A heap of size K finds them in O(n log k) -- without ever fully sorting the other n-k elements you don't care about.

title: Transfer: K Closest Points to the Origin
oneLiner: Keep the k points nearest (0, 0). Same capped heap as Top-K, but now you want the smallest keys, so the heap has to evict the largest.

title: K-way Merge: Merge K Sorted Arrays
oneLiner: Merge k sorted arrays into one by keeping only each array's current head in a min-heap: the heap's top is always the next value of the output.

title: Two Heaps: Median of a Data Stream
oneLiner: Keep the smaller half of the numbers in a max-heap and the larger half in a min-heap; the median is always sitting on top of one or both.

title: Design: Min Stack
oneLiner: A stack that can also tell you its smallest element at any moment, with every operation in O(1).

title: Design: LRU Cache
oneLiner: A fixed-size cache that throws out the least recently used entry when it's full -- with get and put both in O(1).

title: Trees: Validate a Binary Search Tree
oneLiner: Pass an allowed (low, high) range down the tree; every node must fall strictly inside the range its ancestors set.

title: Transfer: Kth Smallest Value in a BST
oneLiner: The BST rule you validated is now a promise: walk the tree inorder, which visits values in sorted order, and stop at the kth one.

title: Trees: Diameter of a Binary Tree
oneLiner: Post-order DFS that returns each subtree's height to its parent while updating a global best path length on the side.

title: Trees: Lowest Common Ancestor
oneLiner: Each call reports back whether it found p or q below it; the first node that hears "found" from both sides is the answer.

title: Union-Find: Count Connected Components
oneLiner: Instead of re-traversing the graph from scratch every time a new connection arrives, union-find merges two groups in almost constant time and remembers the merge forever.

title: Transfer: Redundant Connection
oneLiner: A tree got one extra edge. Find the edge to remove. Union-find again, watching for the one union whose two ends are already connected.

title: Grid Flood Fill: Number of Islands
oneLiner: Scan a 0/1 map; every time you hit unvisited land, count one island and flood-fill all of it so you never count it again.

title: Transfer: Largest Island Area
oneLiner: Same 0/1 map as Number of Islands, changed question: how many cells does the biggest island have? Make the flood fill count what it sinks.

title: Multi-Source BFS: Rotting Oranges
oneLiner: Start a BFS from EVERY rotten orange at once; each BFS layer is one minute, and the answer is how many layers it takes to reach every fresh orange.

title: Minimum Spanning Tree (Kruskal's Algorithm)
oneLiner: Connect every node as cheaply as possible: take edges cheapest-first, skipping any that would close a loop.

title: Topological Sort: Order Tasks by Dependency
oneLiner: Given a pile of tasks with prerequisites, find a valid order to do them in -- or discover there isn't one, because some of them depend on each other in a loop.

title: Transfer: Fewest Semesters to Finish Every Course
oneLiner: Take as many courses per semester as you like, once their prerequisites are done. How many semesters? Kahn's algorithm, counted in layers.

title: Cycle Detection: Course Schedule
oneLiner: Can every course be finished? Only if the prerequisite graph has no cycle, and a DFS that remembers which nodes are on its current path finds one.

title: Graph Traversal + Hash Map: Clone a Graph
oneLiner: Deep-copy a graph that has cycles: walk it once, and keep a map from each original node to its copy so you never copy a node twice.

title: Transfer: Copy a List with Random Pointers
oneLiner: Deep-copy a linked list where every node also has a pointer to any node in the list (or null). The map from Clone a Graph does the work again.

title: BFS on an Implicit Graph: Word Ladder
oneLiner: The fewest one-letter changes from one word to another: the words are nodes, "differs by one letter" is an edge, and BFS finds the shortest path.

title: Graph 2-Colouring: Is a Graph Bipartite?
oneLiner: Can the nodes be split into two groups so every edge crosses between them? Try to colour the graph with two colours and see whether any edge ends up with both ends the same.

title: 1-D DP: House Robber
oneLiner: Pick values from a row to maximize the total, never taking two neighbors -- decided one house at a time with two numbers.

title: Transfer: House Robber on a Circular Street
oneLiner: Same no-two-neighbours rule, but the houses form a circle. Break the circle into two straight streets and reuse the linear answer.

title: State-Machine DP: Stock Trading with Cooldown
oneLiner: Buy and sell as often as you like, but after a sale you must wait a day -- track the best profit for each state you could be in, day by day.

title: 0/1 Knapsack: The Shape Behind Subset-Sum Problems
oneLiner: Pick a subset of items, each usable at most once, to maximize value within a weight limit -- one descending loop is the entire difference from letting an item be reused.

title: Unbounded Knapsack: Coin Change
oneLiner: The fewest coins that add up to an amount, when you can use each coin as many times as you like.

title: Transfer: Coin Change II, Count the Ways
oneLiner: How many different combinations of coins make the amount? The same unbounded table as Coin Change, with min swapped for a sum and the loops in a deliberate order.

title: 2-D DP: Edit Distance
oneLiner: The fewest single-character inserts, deletes and replaces to turn one word into another -- the classic two-string DP table.

title: 2-D DP: Longest Common Subsequence
oneLiner: The longest sequence of characters that appears in both strings in the same order (not necessarily adjacent) -- filled cell by cell in a prefix-by-prefix table.

title: Trie: Prefix Search
oneLiner: A tree of characters where every word that shares a prefix shares the path -- so "how many words start with app?" is one walk, not a scan.

title: Transfer: Replace Words with Their Shortest Root
oneLiner: Replace every word in a sentence by the shortest dictionary root it starts with. Same trie, but now you look for a stored word that is a prefix of the query.

title: Hash Map: Group Anagrams
oneLiner: Give every word a key that all of its anagrams share, then let a hash map do the grouping in one pass.

title: String Matching: KMP Search
oneLiner: Find every occurrence of a pattern in O(n + m) by precomputing, for each prefix of the pattern, how much of it can be reused after a mismatch.

title: Backtracking: Generate All Subsets
oneLiner: Recursion with a choice at every step: include this element or don't, then undo and try the other branch.

title: Transfer: Subsets When the Input Has Duplicates
oneLiner: Every distinct subset of a list that may repeat values, each exactly once: the same backtracking, plus one rule about equal siblings.

title: Backtracking: Generate All Permutations
oneLiner: Fill one position at a time with any number not used yet, recurse, then un-use it and try the next.

title: Backtracking on a Grid: Word Search
oneLiner: Try to spell the word from every cell: step into a matching neighbour, mark it used, recurse, and unmark it on the way back so other paths can use it.

title: Backtracking with Pruning: N-Queens
oneLiner: Place one queen per row; in each row try every column that no earlier queen attacks, recurse, then remove the queen and try the next column.

title: Bit Manipulation: Count Set Bits
oneLiner: AND, OR, XOR, shifts -- the low-level operations bit-manipulation problems are built from, demonstrated by counting a number's 1 bits.

title: Greedy Algorithms: When the Best Next Step Is Enough
oneLiner: Take the locally best choice and never look back: how to tell when that's safe, how to prove it with an exchange argument, and the classic cases where it fails.

title: Greedy: Assign Cookies
oneLiner: Sort the children and the cookies, then give each cookie to the least greedy child it can satisfy.

title: Greedy: Jump Game
oneLiner: Can you reach the last index? Track the farthest index reachable so far in one left-to-right pass.

title: Greedy: Jump Game II (Fewest Jumps)
oneLiner: The fewest jumps to the last index: treat each jump as a BFS level and grow the next level as far as it can go.

title: Greedy: Gas Station
oneLiner: Find the station to start a full loop from: if the tank ever goes negative, no station up to here can be the start.

title: Greedy: Partition Labels
oneLiner: Cut a string into as many pieces as possible so each letter lives in one piece: record each letter's last index, then close a piece when you reach the furthest last index seen.

title: Greedy: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
oneLiner: The largest sum of any contiguous run: a running sum that has gone negative only drags the next element down, so drop it and start fresh.

title: Transfer: Maximum Product Subarray
oneLiner: The largest product of a contiguous run. Kadane's one pass still works, but a negative number flips big and small, so track the smallest run ending here as well as the largest.

title: Math for Coding Interviews: Modulo, GCD, Primes, Powers and Overflow
oneLiner: The number theory and counting that interview problems quietly assume: remainders (and how C# and Python disagree on negatives), Euclid's GCD, the sieve, fast power, overflow and nCr.

title: Math: Count Primes (Sieve of Eratosthenes)
oneLiner: Count the primes below n by crossing out multiples instead of testing each number on its own.

title: Math: Pow(x, n) by Fast Exponentiation
oneLiner: Compute x to the power n in O(log n) multiplications by squaring, and survive n = int.MinValue in C#.

title: Math: GCD and LCM of an Array (Euclid's Algorithm)
oneLiner: Fold Euclid's gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) across the array, and build the LCM as a / gcd * b so it doesn't overflow.

title: Math: Happy Number (Digit Math and Cycle Detection)
oneLiner: Repeatedly replace n by the sum of the squares of its digits; it either reaches 1 or loops forever, and a seen-set or Floyd's two pointers tells which.

title: Math: Excel Column Title (Base 26 With No Zero)
oneLiner: Turn 1, 2, ..., 26, 27 into A, B, ..., Z, AA: base-26 conversion where the digits run 1 to 26, so subtract 1 before each step.

title: Math: Reverse Integer (Overflow and Negative Modulo)
oneLiner: Reverse a 32-bit integer's digits, returning 0 if the result doesn't fit: the lesson where C# and Python disagree about both % and overflow.

title: Bit Manipulation Toolkit: Two's Complement, Masks, Shifts and XOR
oneLiner: How integers really look in binary, the handful of operators that work on those bits, the tricks interviews reuse, and where C# and Python behave differently.

title: Bits: Single Number (XOR Cancels Pairs)
oneLiner: Every value appears twice except one: XOR everything together and the pairs cancel, leaving the single one.

title: Bits: Missing Number
oneLiner: n distinct numbers from 0..n, one missing: XOR every index and every value together and the only thing that doesn't cancel is the missing number.

title: Bits: Power of Two
oneLiner: A power of two has exactly one 1 bit, and n & (n - 1) clears the lowest 1 bit, so n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0 answers it in O(1).

title: Bits: Counting Bits for 0 to n
oneLiner: Return the number of 1 bits in every number from 0 to n in one O(n) pass, reusing the answer for i >> 1.

title: Bits: Reverse Bits of a 32-bit Unsigned Integer
oneLiner: Mirror all 32 bits: pop the lowest bit of n, push it onto the result from the right, exactly 32 times.

title: Bits: Sum of Two Integers Without + or -
oneLiner: Add like a circuit does: XOR is the sum without carries, AND shifted left is the carry, and you repeat until there's no carry left.

title: Bits: All Subsets by Counting Bitmasks
oneLiner: Every number from 0 to 2^n - 1 is a different subset: bit i set means "take nums[i]". Count through them in order.

title: Range Queries: Prefix Sums vs Segment Trees vs Fenwick Trees
oneLiner: Why prefix sums stop working once the array changes, and how a segment tree and a Fenwick tree give O(log n) updates and queries, stepped through node by node.

title: Lazy Propagation, and Choosing a Range-Query Structure
oneLiner: How a segment tree handles "add x to a whole range" in O(log n) by postponing work, and a decision guide for prefix sums, difference arrays, sparse tables, Fenwick trees and segment trees.

title: Segment Tree: Range Sum Query, Mutable
oneLiner: Design a NumArray that supports update(index, val) and sumRange(left, right) on a changing array, both in O(log n).

title: Segment Tree: Range Minimum Query with Updates
oneLiner: Design a RangeMinTree with update(index, val) and queryMin(left, right), both O(log n): the case a Fenwick tree can't handle.

title: Fenwick Tree: Range Add, Point Query
oneLiner: Design a RangeAdder with addRange(left, right, delta) and get(index), both O(log n), by keeping a difference array inside a Fenwick tree.

title: Fenwick Tree: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
oneLiner: For each element, count how many elements to its right are strictly smaller, in O(n log n), with a Fenwick tree indexed by value.

title: Fenwick Tree: Count Inversions in an Array
oneLiner: Count the pairs i < j with nums[i] > nums[j] in O(n log n), using a Fenwick tree of seen values (or merge sort), and return it as a 64-bit number.

oneLiner: Read a problem in plain English and name the technique -- no code, just the reflex that decides whether you freeze in an interview.

title: Mixed Interview Set: Unlabeled Problems Against the Clock
oneLiner: Random problems from the graded lessons with the titles and hints stripped off, on an interview timer.

title: OOP Basics: Classes, Objects, and Polymorphism
oneLiner: The same "compute a shape's area" problem, solved two ways -- one where adding a new shape means editing existing code, and one where it doesn't.

title: Interfaces & Abstraction: Program to a Contract, Not an Implementation
oneLiner: Calling code that only knows about an interface never needs to change when a new implementation shows up -- this app is a live example of exactly that.

title: Services & Dependency Injection: Handed Dependencies, Not Constructed Ones
oneLiner: A class that builds its own dependencies is stuck with them forever; a class that receives its dependencies through its constructor (the special method that runs when an object is created with new) can be handed a completely different one without changing a single line.

oneLiner: Not the full Gang-of-Four catalog (the 1994 book by four authors that named 23 classic patterns) -- just four patterns that show up constantly in real code, including this app's own.

oneLiner: Each principle as a before and after in C#, plus the code smell that tells you it is being broken.

oneLiner: Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Singleton and Prototype, each with C#, a real .NET example and the interview angle.

title: Structural Patterns: Wrapping and Composing Objects
oneLiner: Adapter, Decorator, Facade, Proxy and Composite: five ways to put one object in front of, around or inside another.

oneLiner: Strategy, Observer, Command, State, Template Method, Iterator and Chain of Responsibility, with C# and the .NET features built on them.

oneLiner: N floors, M cars: which car answers a call, what order a car stops in, and how fire mode fits in later.

title: Design a Deck of Cards and Blackjack (OOD)
oneLiner: A reusable deck, then Blackjack on top of it: scoring aces, the dealer's rule, a round of play, and splits as the follow-up.

oneLiner: The four clauses that answer 90% of "get me some rows" questions: which columns, which rows, in what order, how many.

title: SQL Joins: Combining Tables
oneLiner: Real data lives in more than one table on purpose -- a JOIN is how you ask a question that spans both without duplicating data everywhere.

title: SQL Aggregation: GROUP BY, COUNT, SUM, AVG
oneLiner: Answering "how many" and "what's the average, per group" without writing a loop -- GROUP BY collapses many rows into one summary row per group.

title: Schema Design: Keys, Constraints & Normalization
oneLiner: Store each fact once, and make the database itself refuse data that breaks your rules.

title: SQL Indexes & Query Plans

title: SQL Transactions & ACID
oneLiner: A bank transfer is two UPDATEs. A transaction is what stops a crash between them from losing money.

oneLiner: Remotes, pull requests, code review, merge versus squash versus rebase, and what to do when your push is rejected.

oneLiner: Every network request is really several layers wrapping each other's output -- each one only has to understand its own layer, not the whole stack.

title: IP Addressing & Subnetting
oneLiner: An IP + a subnet mask splits into a network portion and a host portion -- CIDR (/24) is just how many bits belong to the network.

title: Subnetting Practice: Unlimited Drills
oneLiner: Generated subnetting questions without end: network and broadcast addresses, host counts, masks, sizing a subnet, same-subnet checks and private ranges, each with a worked answer.

title: MAC Addresses, ARP and Switches
oneLiner: How a frame actually reaches the device next to you: MAC addresses, the ARP question "who has this IP?", and a switch learning which port each device is on.

title: VLANs: Several Networks on One Switch
oneLiner: Split one physical switch into separate networks for office, production and guests, carry them all on one cable with tags, and route between them under firewall rules.

title: DHCP: How Devices Get an Address
oneLiner: Plug in a laptop and it has an address, mask, gateway and DNS server within a second. Step through the four DHCP messages, lease renewal, and the classic failures: an empty pool, a 169.254 address and a rogue server.

title: Wi-Fi Basics: Bands, Channels, Signal and Security
oneLiner: Why Wi-Fi slows down when it's busy, why channels 1, 6 and 11, what -67 dBm means, and which security mode a company network should use.

title: Routing and Default Gateways
oneLiner: How a PC decides whether a destination is local or must go to the router, and how a router picks the next hop: masks, the default gateway, routing tables and longest prefix match.

title: NAT and Port Forwarding
oneLiner: How a whole office shares one public IP address, why the internet can't reach your devices unless you forward a port, and why port forwarding often fails behind carrier-grade NAT.

title: TCP vs UDP: Reliable vs Fire-and-Forget
oneLiner: Same job -- get data from one program to another over IP -- two completely different guarantees about whether it actually arrives, in order, or at all.

title: DNS & HTTP: From a URL to a Web Page
oneLiner: Typing a URL and seeing a page triggers a whole chain of lookups and handshakes underneath -- this is that chain, one step at a time.

title: Firewalls and Ports
oneLiner: An ordered rule list in front of a production network: first match wins, default deny, and why stateful firewalls let replies back. Plus drop versus reject, what's listening, and the port numbers worth knowing.

title: VPNs and Tunnels
oneLiner: What a VPN actually does to your packets, what someone on café Wi-Fi can still see, full versus split tunnel, and site-to-site versus remote access.

title: Network Troubleshooting Toolkit
oneLiner: Six support tickets, each a different fault in a real lab network. Run ip, ping, traceroute, nslookup, curl and ss, read the real output, and name the cause.

title: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
oneLiner: Turn users and actions into requests per second, storage and bandwidth in a few lines of rounded arithmetic.

title: Load Balancing
oneLiner: How a load balancer spreads requests across servers, and what goes wrong when requests differ in cost or a server dies.

title: Caching
oneLiner: Keep a copy of hot data somewhere fast, and decide how stale that copy is allowed to get.

title: CDNs and Edge Caching
oneLiner: Serve bytes from a city near the user instead of from your datacenter: points of presence, cache keys, Cache-Control headers, invalidation and origin shields.

title: Replication and Sharding
oneLiner: Copy your data to survive failures and serve more reads, and split it to handle more writes and more data than one machine can hold.

title: Consistent Hashing
oneLiner: Spread keys over servers so that adding or removing a server moves only a small fraction of them.

title: Message Queues
oneLiner: Put a buffer between the service that produces work and the one that does it, and plan for every message arriving twice.

title: Distributed Async Systems: Streams, Outbox and Sagas
oneLiner: Work queues vs pub/sub vs Kafka-style logs, consumer groups and offsets, idempotency keys, the transactional outbox, sagas and ordering guarantees.

title: Rate Limiting
oneLiner: Four ways to cap how many requests a client can make, compared on the same traffic.

title: CAP and Consistency
oneLiner: When the network between your copies breaks, you choose between refusing requests and serving answers that may be wrong.

title: Tail Latency and Request Hedging
oneLiner: Why the slowest 1% of calls decides how fast a large system feels, and how a backup request fixes it for a few percent more load.

title: Timeouts, Retries, Circuit Breakers and Load Shedding
oneLiner: How a five-second slowdown becomes an outage that outlives it when every client retries at once, and the patterns that stop it.

title: Observability and SLOs
oneLiner: Logs, metrics and traces, then SLIs, SLOs, error budgets and burn-rate alerts, with the RED and USE methods for knowing what to measure.

title: Scale It Yourself: a Traffic Simulator Lab
oneLiner: Add load balancers, caches, replicas, a CDN, queues and a rate limiter to a web service under rising load and failures, and watch latency, errors, saturation and cost.

title: REST Resources and HTTP Semantics
oneLiner: Nouns in the URL, verbs in the method, outcomes in the status code: what each HTTP method promises and why retries depend on it.

title: REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL
oneLiner: Three ways to shape the same API, compared on round trips, bytes on the wire and who carries the complexity.

title: Pagination: Offset vs Cursor
oneLiner: Why page 2 shows posts you already saw when new ones arrive, and how a cursor fixes it and stays fast on page 10,000.

title: Idempotency Keys and Safe Retries

title: Versioning, Compatibility and Error Formats

title: API Keys, OAuth Scopes, Rate Limits and Quotas
oneLiner: The checks every request passes before your handler runs: who is calling, what they may do, to which object, and how often.

oneLiner: WhatsApp or Messenger as a 45-minute design round: long-lived connections, ordering, receipts and offline delivery.

oneLiner: A distributed API rate limiter as a 45-minute design round: algorithms, atomic counters in Redis, and what happens when the limiter fails.

title: Design a Distributed Key-Value Store
oneLiner: Dynamo or Cassandra as a 45-minute design round: consistent hashing, quorums, conflict resolution, repair and LSM storage.

title: Design a Web Crawler
oneLiner: A search engine crawler as a 45-minute design round: the URL frontier, politeness, deduplication and recrawl scheduling.

oneLiner: Push, SMS and email for many product teams as a 45-minute design round: priority, provider limits, retries and duplicates.

oneLiner: YouTube as a 45-minute design round: resumable uploads, a parallel transcoding pipeline, adaptive streaming and a CDN that carries tens of terabits per second.

oneLiner: Uber or Lyft as a 45-minute design round: live driver locations, geospatial search, dispatch, and a trip that is never double-booked.

title: Design a Distributed Job Scheduler
oneLiner: Run millions of one-off and recurring jobs on time across a fleet of workers, as a 45-minute design round: leases, retries, at-least-once and no double runs that matter.

title: Design a Payment System
oneLiner: Take payments for an online marketplace through an external payment processor, as a 45-minute design round: idempotency, exactly-once effects, a ledger and reconciliation.

oneLiner: Name, build, store and ship container images safely: registries, tags and digests, multi-stage builds and image hygiene.

title: Kubernetes in Practice: Labels, Services, Probes and kubectl
oneLiner: The Kubernetes objects you use every day, how they find each other, and how to work out why a pod isn't running.

title: CI/CD Pipelines

oneLiner: Find out what's wrong in a running system: percentiles, structured logs, distributed traces and alerts worth waking up for.

oneLiner: Why models read tokens rather than words or characters, how byte-pair encoding builds a vocabulary, and how embeddings turn each token into a vector where similar meanings sit close together.

oneLiner: The architecture behind today's language models: every token looks at the other tokens to decide what it means here, and the model predicts one next token at a time inside a fixed context window.

oneLiner: Find the passwords and keys hiding in a repository, learn where secrets should live instead, then cut a service account's database rights down to exactly what its job needs.

oneLiner: The ten most important web application security risks, in both the 2021 and 2025 editions, each with an everyday example, the fix, and where this academy covers it.

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
oneLiner: SQL injection's cousin in the browser: user input that ends up running as code in someone else's page.

oneLiner: Three ways an attacker uses access they shouldn't have: changing an ID in a URL, getting your browser to send a request for them, and getting the server to fetch internal addresses.

oneLiner: Why letting incoming data pick its own type can run an attacker's choice of code, and a pre-go-live review where you hunt for the settings that leave an app exposed.

oneLiner: Draw what the system does, then ask six questions of every part of it: can someone spoof it, tamper with it, deny it, read it, stop it, or gain power through it?

title: Phishing and Social Engineering
oneLiner: Sort a practice inbox into phishing and genuine mail, learn the red flags that give attackers away, and how the same tricks arrive by phone, text, USB stick and at the door.

oneLiner: PLC memory isn't a flat address space the way a general computer's RAM is -- it's organized into named REGIONS by what kind of thing each bit represents.

oneLiner: How does a PLC actually talk to an HMI (human-machine interface: the operator's screen), a SCADA (supervisory control and data acquisition) system that monitors a whole site, or another PLC? Usually with a protocol built around one machine ASKING and another ANSWERING, not the general internet's anyone-can-initiate model.

title: Safety & Redundancy: Designing for What Happens When It Fails

oneLiner: Make a lamp flash half a second on, half a second off, using on-delay timers that restart themselves.

title: Exercise: Debounce a Bouncy Contact
oneLiner: Filter contact bounce out of a switch signal: only accept a change once the input has been steady for 50 ms, in both directions.

title: Edge Detection: R_TRIG, F_TRIG and One-Scan Pulses
oneLiner: Levels vs edges: why a held button is TRUE for hundreds of scans, how R_TRIG and F_TRIG turn a change into a pulse that lasts exactly one scan, and the ladder and hand-written equivalents.

title: Exercise: Push-On, Push-Off Toggle
oneLiner: One pushbutton turns a lamp on, the next press turns it off. Easy to describe, and a classic trap for code that acts on the level instead of the edge.

title: Counters: CTU, CTD and CTUD
oneLiner: Up, down and up/down counters: they count rising edges, not scans; reset and load take priority; and the outputs flag when a preset is reached.

title: Exercise: Tank Level with Hysteresis and Alarm
oneLiner: Run a fill pump between 20 % and 80 % with hysteresis, and raise a high level alarm with a deadband, so neither chatters around a single threshold.

oneLiner: Habits that make PLC programs safe to run and easy to fix: clear names and comments, one place per output, interlocks, fail-safe wiring and defaults, testing, and why safety functions belong in safety-rated hardware, not a standard program.

oneLiner: Run a press only while two buttons are held, pressed within half a second of each other, and refuse to restart until both are released.
